title: Training-Inference Consistent Segmented Execution for Long-Context LLMs

claims.claim: The framework defines segment-level execution semantics where training and inference process sequences segment by segment with the same cross-segment interface (Definition 3.1)
observations: The local surrogate uses one segment operator for all segment steps.
The carried state interface is identical in the TBPTT and explicit truncated-objective checks.

claims.claim: For the stated truncated consistent objective, TBPTT computes the exact gradient rather than an approximation (Theorem 3.3)
observations: Maximum absolute gradient error between TBPTT and explicit truncated objective: 0.000e+00.

claims.claim: Training-inference alignment follows when the same segmented execution semantics and truncated objective are used for training and inference (Corollary 3.4)
observations: The executable check aligns training and inference semantics in a small deterministic recurrence.
This supports the formal mechanism but does not reproduce a trained long-context LLM.

claims.claim: The architecture uses head- and layer-sparse long-range retrieval with carried KV tails and forward-only retrieved prefixes (Figure 3)
observations: Retrieved prefixes change the forward output while their gradient norm remains zero.

claims.claim: The method achieves comparable LongBench-E performance while lowering prefill memory and latency relative to full-context attention and other efficient baselines (Table 1)
observations: No released LongBench-E outputs, model checkpoints, or executable benchmark scripts were found.
The evidence does not treat table values from the paper as reproduced measurements.

claims.claim: At 128K context, segmented execution provides approximately 6x lower peak prefill memory than full-context attention with FlashAttention (Figure 5)
observations: Analytic peak-memory proxy gives a 128K full/segmented ratio of 6.007.
This validates scaling direction only, not the paper's FlashAttention GPU measurement.
